# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the mug positioned to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows the mug positioned to the right of the headphones; fail if it clearly shows the mug is not to their right; unknown if their relative position cannot be determined. For R1, complete if this check passes; absent if it fails and no requested change has progressed; partial if the mug has moved toward the requested position but is not yet to the right; unknown if required evidence remains unresolved. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Compare the mug’s visible position with the headphones in the image. Judge the requested spatial relationship, without requiring a particular editing technique.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the visible mug is positioned to the right of the headphones.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image clearly shows a mug and headphones, and their relative positions are observable: the mug is to the right of the headphones. Both objects are identifiable enough for comparison.

fulfillment: The binding is too broad and the node treats the final spatial relation as sufficient proof of fulfillment. In the edited image, a mug is indeed to the right of the headphones, but the source shows the mug on their left; the edit also leaves a mug-like object on the left and introduces a conspicuous blurred blue remnant. Thus the requested move appears to have progressed, but the image does not clearly establish that the original mug was moved cleanly or that the requested edit is complete. Make the node compare the same target and reference across source and edited snapshots, and distinguish partial progress from complete fulfillment while applying the rubric; do not infer absence from the artifacts or unrelated changes. The two support observations are highly confident but appear to repeat the same final-image relation, not independently verify change or completion. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported, so investigate the semantic evidence and criterion application rather than execution.

response.content: {"text":"The binding checks only whether some visible mug is right of the headphones, so it can pass on a newly introduced mug while ignoring whether the source mug moved. Bind the comparison to the same identifiable target across source and edited snapshots, and assess its displacement relative to the headphones. Keep the spatial-relation check distinct from the fulfillment criterion: a right-side mug alone does not establish that the requested move is complete when the source mug remains on the left and a blurred blue remnant is visible. Use the rubric to distinguish demonstrated progress from completion, and leave the result unresolved if target identity or movement cannot be established; do not treat artifacts as proof of no progress. The repeated high-confidence observations support only the final-image relation, not independent evidence of change. This is a semantic binding/evidence issue, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure."}
